newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via overnight system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via overnight system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to inject temporary reserves into the banking system on Tuesday through a round of overnight system repurchase agreements.
The Fed executed $2.17 billion worth of overnight system RPs on Monday, which surprised some analysts looking for a longer term (10-day) and larger amount.
Some analysts admitted that they may have overestimated the Fed's add job a bit, which is projected to face less than the previously forecast $6.5 billion a day.
Plus, the Fed is being cautious about its add job and is likely taking it one day at a time, analysts added.

The add need is expected to rise in the second half of the maintenance period, beginning on Thursday, as corporate and estimated second quarter estimated tax receipts pour into the Treasury, thereby raising its balance and draining Fed reserves.
As such, analysts predict the Fed will add permanent reserves thorugh an outright purchase of bills, although the timing is up in the air.
Fed funds were at 5-7/16 percent, just below the Fed's 5-1.2 percent target rate.
